header: Date: 2026-04-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Redwood Solutions); Priya Rao (Sable Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Sable Platform), Leah Kim (Sable SecOps), Jon Erickson (Sable Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on prefetch/kv and prefix reuse. Reviewed last week's KV hit improvements (from 18% -> 36% for top-100 prefixes), discussed anomalous eviction patterns under burst, and clarified security requirements for Private deployment. Agreed next steps: share raw hit-rate exports, customer to send canonical prompts, schedule security deep dive.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 45 minutes, quick agenda — metric sync, tuning notes, security, next steps
00:12 Priya Rao: thanks Maya, we swapped timelines a bit so appreciate the short agenda, quick note — LN we had a surprise last night with low hit on support flows
00:25 Liam O'Neill: (SE) yeah we saw a dip, initial analysis shows prefix fragmentation; top prefixes had good reuse but tail is very long
00:38 Carlos Mendes: can you remind which model variant you're running on the pilot? is it redwood-ggml-7b or the quantized 13b? there's been some confusion in the doc
00:50 Maya Chen: we're on the 13b-q4hq per our pilot plan, but with fallback to 7b for burst. docs might say 7b in one place, sorry about that
01:05 Priya Rao: okay that matches what we thought. main ask today: we want predictable cost under peak; hit rate matters a lot for our math
01:18 Liam O'Neill: quick slide — last 7 days top-100 prefixes hh, overall kv hit was 36% yesterday up from 18% two weeks ago. big win from changing prefix normalization and tokenization alignment
01:35 Jon Erickson: can you explain tokenization alignment? that's been fuzzy across teams
01:47 Liam O'Neill: yeah, basically we normalized whitespace and removed stop tokens before keying; also we moved to a 64-token prefix window instead of 128, which increased reuse for short Q/A flows
02:05 Leah Kim: small callout on security — any raw prompts in cache? we need assurance about PII and retention and how KMS wraps those keys
02:18 Arjun Patel: important point. in Redwood Private the KV cache lives in customer VPC and we can opt to not persist to disk; KMS enforced access and we have TTL-based eviction
02:33 Leah Kim: low confidence from SecOps, we'll need an architecture diagram and whether audit logs capture cache hits/evictions
02:47 Maya Chen: noted — action: we'll share the cache architecture diagram and audit log sample. Liam will pull the per-key audit sample
03:10 Priya Rao: on the metrics, the top prefixes look great, but our user flows have a long tail — does the runtime do any probabilistic prefetching or cohort warmup?
03:25 Liam O'Neill: we have heuristic prefetch: session-cohort warmup where we precompute next likely prefixes for repeated sessions, and also time-decay scoring. but with high cardinality inputs it doesn't help much
03:40 Carlos Mendes: during burst yesterday we saw eviction thrashing, some prefixes were getting evicted then re-added repeatedly — thought that would hurt latency more than token cost
03:58 Arjun Patel: yep that's eviction churn, common when the on-heap budget is small. options: increase cache memory, tune eviction thresholds, or adjust prefetch aggressiveness
04:14 Priya Rao: what's the latency hit when cache miss goes to model? we need p95 numbers for the plan
04:25 Liam O'Neill: p95 cold path to 13b-q4hq is ~420ms on our dedicated pilot nodes; with warm KV hit we drop to ~95-120ms depending on response length
04:41 Jon Erickson: so doubled cost for misses plus latency penalty. that checks out with our internal calc
04:55 Maya Chen: tradeoff note: more aggressive prefetch reduces misses but increases compute egress for prefetched tokens, so we need a cost curve
05:12 Liam O'Neill: we prepared a small cost-vs-hit curve — can upload; also per-prefix marginal benefit numbers
05:25 Priya Rao: yes please upload; we want to test a conservative prefetch window first
05:37 Carlos Mendes: question on prompt reuse — some of our prompts include ephemeral session IDs that kill keying. what do you recommend
05:49 Liam O'Neill: remove ephemeral id from key; we suggest a canonicalization pass. we can provide a snippet to strip or hash certain fields and keep structural tokens
06:05 Priya Rao: perfect, we can run that on edge. will that change hit distribution significantly
06:14 Liam O'Neill: in our tests canonicalization of session-id increased top-500 prefix hit by 12-15% in similar corpora
06:27 Leah Kim: security follow-up — if we canonicalize, are we changing data retention semantics? need to confirm revocation paths
06:39 Arjun Patel: canonicalization is at pre-key layer, you can choose to not log raw input. revocation still applies because the cache TTLs control lifecycles; we can also rotate keys
06:53 Priya Rao: on TTLs what's the recommended window for support flows? these are often stateful conversations over 10-20 minutes
07:05 Liam O'Neill: for support flows we use 30-minute TTL with session-affinity hints; for high-frequency bot flows 5-10 minutes is fine
07:18 Carlos Mendes: we tried 30 minutes but saw memory growth and evictions; maybe our session id fragmentation was the root cause
07:31 Maya Chen: action item — Liam to run a simulation of 30 vs 10 minute TTL on their sample traffic and show mem usage
07:45 Liam O'Neill: will do, simulation + heatmap
07:51 Jon Erickson: a tangent — competitor benchmarking, do we have any numbers? Anthropic seemed to have a larger external cache offering
08:02 Maya Chen: we have rough public numbers but our angle is runtime integration and lower tail latency; we'll send a comparison note
08:14 Priya Rao: procurement is asking about SLAs if we move to Dedicated; also compliance for EU data residency
08:26 Maya Chen: Dedicated offers SLA-backed capacity and region pinning; Private gives full control over residency. Leah, we should sync on compliance docs
08:40 Leah Kim: yes, please send SOC2 type II evidence, ISO attestation, and the KMS integration diagram
08:51 Arjun Patel: note: in Private there's a customer-managed KMS option, and audit logs are shipped to customer SIEM
09:05 Carlos Mendes: for the prefetch algorithm, is it deterministic? we worry about non-deterministic prefetch causing flakiness in A/B tests
09:16 Liam O'Neill: it's heuristic but tunable and you can lock seeds for determinism; we'll show the knob settings
09:28 Priya Rao: good, we'd like a canary with deterministic prefetch first
09:36 Maya Chen: agreed. next steps we'll schedule a canary rollout and then a wider pilot
09:45 Liam O'Neill: quick clarification: what does Sable define as success at end of POC? hit-rate target + latency p95 < 200ms for core flows?
09:56 Priya Rao: yes, target 45% KV hit for core flows and p95 < 200ms with 80th percentile of responses under 120ms. also cost per session under X (we'll share exact number)
10:15 Maya Chen: perfect. I'll capture that in the deal notes. any blockers from your side on timeline
10:25 Jon Erickson: we'll get canonical prompt set and traffic dist by 2026-05-05; security will review and revert by 2026-05-04
10:38 Leah Kim: one ask — sample audit log with obfuscated entries so SecOps can confirm fields
10:49 Arjun Patel: noted. we'll prepare an obfuscated audit snippet
11:01 Maya Chen: recap: Liam send hit-rate csv + simulation; Maya send pricing sketch; customer send prompts and traffic; security docs exchange; schedule security deep dive 2026-05-07
11:22 Priya Rao: sounds good, thanks all
11:25 (end) Speaker 1: thanks everyone
11:28 (end) Speaker 2: bye
